body:
WHAT
As assistant text streams in, the renderer commits every complete Markdown block — text up to the last blank line whose preceding fences (``` / ~~~) and `$$` delimiters are balanced — as rendered Markdown, and keeps the unfinished tail as plain text. A half-streamed code fence, table or display formula therefore stays plain until its closing delimiter arrives. On finish the whole message is re-rendered once.

WHY
Rendering everything at the end left long answers as raw source for the whole turn, and rendering partial constructs made them flicker between parses.

WHERE
app/renderer/modules/stream.js — markdownCommitPoint(raw), commitStreamedMarkdown(el) (uses el._raw, el._committedLen, .md-done and .md-live children), finalizeAssistantEl(). app/renderer/modules/markdown.js — renderMarkdown(md) (fence branch consumes to closing fence, display math branch, tableStartsAt()/makeTable(), paragraph splitting), renderInline().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. markdownCommitPoint('para one

```js
let x

more') returns 'para one
' — the cut inside the open fence is rejected and the earlier blank line is used.
2. markdownCommitPoint('$$
a+b

') returns '' (unbalanced $$), while markdownCommitPoint('$$a$$

tail') returns '$$a$$
'.
3. After deltas '# Title

' then 'streaming words', .md-done contains an <h1> and .md-live textContent is 'streaming words'; committing again with no new blank line does not re-parse the committed prefix (el._committedLen unchanged).
4. A table header and delimiter row without a trailing blank line stay in .md-live as plain text; once '

' follows, .md-done gains a <table class="md-table">.
5. finalizeAssistantEl replaces .msg-body with a single full renderMarkdown(raw) result, so a block split awkwardly across commits is rendered whole and no .caret remains.
